$comment: Copy and retrieval vocabulary for the assistant on /.
Refusals are decided by src/lib/assistant/prefilter.ts (deterministic, no model).
factConcepts: a verified fact is retrieved when the question contains EVERY concept
listed for it. Each concept is a list of phrases; any phrase counts.
TODO(content): replace handoff.href with the exact EnergyX Investor Relations page once confirmed.

intro.heading: Ask about EnergyX's public information
intro.body: Answers come only from the fact registry: figures EnergyX has published, and Raj's own measurements of its website, each with its source. If a question isn't covered, it says so instead of guessing.
intro.hardRule: This assistant never answers forward-looking or investment questions, not partly and not with caveats. That check runs before any model is involved.

form.label: Your question
form.placeholder: For example: how long does EnergyX's DLE process take?
form.privacy: This demo doesn't store questions. Your question goes in the page address, so the host's request logs may hold it briefly. Don't include personal details.

groups.label: Answered from the registry
questions: How long does EnergyX's DLE process take?
How much water does EnergyX save compared with conventional extraction?
How heavy is the Black Giant page?

ipo.label: a question about an IPO or a stock listing
ipo.title: I can't discuss an IPO or a stock listing.
ipo.why: Whether, when or how a company lists its shares is forward-looking, and what's said about it is tightly regulated, especially while a company is raising money from the public. Anything I said would be speculation presented as information.

future-timing.label: a question about future timing
future-timing.title: I can't tell you when things will happen.
future-timing.why: Dates for future events, such as production starts, launches and completions, are plans, and plans change. If I gave you a date, you might rely on it as if it were a fact. Only EnergyX can tell you what it currently plans and how firm that is.

returns.label: a question about investment returns
returns.title: I can't tell you what an investment might return.
returns.why: Nobody knows future returns. A number or a direction from me would read like a promise, and past figures or company milestones don't tell you what you'd get back.

advice.label: a request for investment advice
advice.title: I can't give investment advice.
advice.why: Whether to invest depends on your money, your goals and how much risk you can take. I know none of that, and I'm not licensed to advise anyone. I can tell you what EnergyX has published, with sources; the decision needs someone who can look at your situation.

valuation.label: a question about valuation or share price
valuation.title: I can't put a value on the company or its shares.
valuation.why: A valuation is an opinion about the future, not a published fact. Share terms in an offering are set out in the offering documents, which I don't summarise. Read them directly or ask Investor Relations.

guarantees.label: a question about safety or guarantees
guarantees.title: I can't call any investment safe or guaranteed.
guarantees.why: That would be a promise about the future, which nobody can honestly make. The offering documents describe the risks as the company sees them.

comparison.label: a comparison with other investments
comparison.title: I can't compare EnergyX with other investments.
comparison.why: Saying one investment is better than another is a recommendation, even when it's phrased as a comparison. It also depends on things about you that I don't know.

offering.label: a question about buying shares
offering.title: I can't help with buying shares.
offering.why: This demo has no investment flow and doesn't summarise offering terms. EnergyX publishes those itself, and its Investor Relations team can take you through them.

planned-figure.label: a question whose answer is a target or estimate
planned-figure.title: That figure is a target, not a result.
planned-figure.why: EnergyX has published a figure for this, but it's a plan or an estimate, and those can change or not happen. I only state measured or reported facts, so I won't give it as an answer. You can read it in its original context here:

handoff.lead: For this, go to EnergyX directly:
handoff.label: energyx.com

no-match.title: I don't have a sourced answer for that.
no-match.body: I only answer from facts that have been checked against a published source, and none of them covers this question.

post-check.title: I don't have a sourced answer for that.
post-check.body: A draft answer included something I couldn't trace back to a sourced fact, so I dropped it rather than show it.

language.title: I can only answer in English.
language.body: The fact registry and its checks are written in English, so I can't reliably answer questions in other languages yet.

empty.title: Ask a question to get started.
empty.body: Type a question about EnergyX's published facts, or pick one of the examples.

too-long.title: Ask one short question.
too-long.body: Long messages are hard to check reliably, so this assistant only accepts short questions.
